Border Corridor — VIIRS/DNB Analysis


Emilio E. Falco
August 2026

Instrument: VIIRS/DNB · VNP46A1
Source: NASA Earthdata
Period: 2020 – 2026
Southern Arizona DarkSky Chapter

The analysis uses the daily NASA Earthdata VNP46A1 atmospherically corrected product at 500 m resolution. To isolate individual sources of light change, I divided the 48 km border strip into five equal segments running W→E along the ORPI southern boundary. Monthly medians are computed from moon-free, cloud-filtered nights only.

Two time periods are shown. The first covers 2020–2023, dominated by a sharp construction-related spike in Segments 4 and 5 in early-to-mid 2021. The second covers 2023–2026, a stable post-construction baseline across all segments.

Methodology
Independent cross-validation

The segment extraction pipeline used throughout this report was independently cross-checked against a geometry-matched Google Earth Engine extraction of the same five segments over 2020–2026. The two pipelines agree closely across all segments (ratio 0.68–1.01, r = 0.56–0.99), and the 2021 construction-period signal in Segments 4 and 5 is confirmed by both independently. Full methodology, per-segment statistics, and comparison plots are in the companion report: ORPI_ours_vs_GEE_cross_validation.docx.

Period 1 · 2020–2023
Border wall construction signal

Monthly medians of nightly radiance sum in nW/cm2/sr for each segment. The dominant feature is a sharp, temporary increase in Segments 4 and 5 (E of Sonoyta and Ali Chuk) during construction lighting in early-to-mid 2021.

VNP46A1 · OrganPipe_20 (2.00 km wide strip) · 2020-01-01 → 2023-01-31 · Monthly medians shown as diamonds

Seg 4 & 5 — 2021 construction spike (Jan–May 2021)

Segments 4 and 5 (E of Sonoyta and Ali Chuk) show a sharp, temporary increase during border wall construction, roughly 4–9x their baseline monthly medians from January through May 2021, then a rapid return to baseline in June 2021. This is the dominant feature in the 2020–2023 record.

Seg 3 — Lukeville / Sonoyta

Segment 3 is persistently the brightest segment throughout this period due to the Lukeville/Sonoyta border crossing. A gradual decline over 2021–2022 may reflect the LED retrofit of municipal streetlighting — likely a spectral artefact in VIIRS rather than true dimming.

Seg 1 — quiescent

No comparable spike near the western end (~Lukeville). Monthly medians drift gradually upward over the full 2020–2023 span, within the expected range of seasonal and cloud-related variability.

Seg 2 — quiescent

Segment 2 shows a modest, broader rise through late 2020 into mid-2021 but nothing approaching the magnitude seen in Segments 4 and 5, and it settles back to baseline over the same window. Undulations in all segments are within the expected variability from cloud contamination and atmospheric variation.

Period 2 · 2023–2026
Post-construction baseline

Monthly medians of nightly radiance sum in nW/cm2/sr for each segment. No segment shows a sustained step-change comparable to the 2021 construction spike in this period; all five segments track close to their pre-construction baselines.

VNP46A1 · OrganPipe_23 (2.00 km wide strip) · 2023-02-01 → 2026-08-26 · Monthly medians shown as diamonds

Segs 1, 3, 4, 5 — stable

No significant activity in 2023–2026. Segments 1, 4, and 5 remain close to their pre-construction baselines. Segment 3 continues at its persistently elevated level from the Lukeville/Sonoyta crossing.

Seg 2 — modest rise in 2025–2026

Segment 2 shows a gradual increase in monthly medians through 2025 into 2026, roughly 20–40% above its 2023–2024 baseline in the later months of the record. This is far smaller than the 2021 construction spike and the source is not yet identified; worth continued monitoring.
